mix_frequency_estimate: AKo class on Qc5c4d 4-way OOP 3-bettor 3-bet pot: BET 25-30% / CHECK 70-75%; AcKd specifically: BET 50-60% / CHECK 40-50%
reasoning:
Multiway 3-bet-pot OOP from PFA (3-bettor) with three villains behind. Bet-frequency at the class level is REDUCED vs HU 3-bet pots because:
  (1) Three ranges contain >0 equity even with a moderate cbet (~67% fold equity in HU = ~30-40% multiway because callers compound).
  (2) Two-tone boards multiway create check-back protection problems on turn — hero loses positional inversion EV in multiway.
  (3) Hero's range advantage shrinks as ranges multiply (CO + SB + UTG cold-call ranges collectively cover more of the board than CO alone would).

That said, the small-cbet (25%) protocol still has a place at this node because:
  (1) Q-high boards favor PFA (3-bettor) range: QQ+/AK have Q for top set/TPTK; villain cold-call ranges lack QQ, AK and have weaker Qx.
  (2) Hero's AKo class includes AcKd which adds Ac-blocker leverage to villains' nut-FD combos.
  (3) Small sizing (25%) keeps SPR high enough for turn flexibility — hero retains check-back protection on bad turns (Jx, Tx connecting).

Villa-by-villain analysis:
  - UTG (opener-then-called-3bet): tight calling-3bet range. TT-99, AQs sometimes, suited broadways, KQs. AK is mostly 4-bet (UTG vs MP) but ~30% mixed call. AA/KK is mostly 4-bet too. Net: UTG range is ~50 combos of medium-strength + ~5 combos of AA/KK/AK call. AcKd vs UTG range on Qc5c4d: ~55-60% equity.
  - CO (cold-call-of-3bet): wider — TT-77, AQs-AJs, KQs, suited connectors 76s+, 87s, suited Ax. AcKd vs CO: ~62%.
  - SB (cold-call-of-3bet): tightest — TT-99, AQs-AJs sometimes, suited broadways. AcKd vs SB: ~58%.
Multiway, AcKd's effective equity is ~38-44%. Equity-realization OOP-vs-3 in 3-bet pot is ~0.80. EV-equity ~31-35%. That's marginal-but-defensible for a small protection cbet.

The Ac-blocker leverage in multiway:
  - Blocks AcXc combos in villain cold-call ranges (AcQc, AcJc, Ac9c, Ac8c — full suited Ac range in CO/SB).
  - Hero's Ac removes ~5-6 of the nut-FD combos per villain → multiplied across 3 villains, ~15-18 nut-FD combos blocked.
  - This MEANINGFULLY reduces villains' continuation density on club turns (the worst turn for hero's no-FD overcards).
  - In multiway, this matters more than HU because hero is more vulnerable to a club turn 3-bet-jam from any villain.

The sizing 66% IS WRONG for multiway. 66% bet in a 3-bet pot OOP into 3 villains is:
  - Inefficient at folding marginal hands (need 40% fold equity = 1.6 fold equity × 3 villains × 50% each = ineffective).
  - Bloats pot OOP — hero loses turn-c/f option (becomes nearly committed at SPR 1.5 turn).
  - Bet too thin for value with AcKd (which is 38-44% equity).
The correct sizing is 25% (range-bet protection). 33% is acceptable. 66% is a labeller error driven by 'AK is value' thinking that doesn't apply on Q-high boards where AK is a thin-value/protection hand, not a polar-value hand.

Paired with pilot 085 (resolved BET 33% via Ac-blocker leverage): 016 differs from 085 in that 085 had Qc4c3s (lower-connected, slightly worse for hero's range), 016 has Qc5c4d (less connected, slightly better for hero's range). If 085 resolved BET, 016 should resolve BET WITH AT LEAST AS HIGH FREQUENCY — the board texture is marginally MORE favorable to PFA range (slightly higher card density, less straight equity for villain SCs).

Verdict: BET 25 at MEDIUM confidence. Action LABEL agrees with consensus; sizing DISAGREES (25, not 66). The 1-of-5 labeller who voted BET 25 was correct on sizing. AcKd combo-level BET frequency ~55-60% via Ac-blocker leverage as in 085.
